⚠ Every week of delay in Phase 2 or 3 pushes your launch by one week. There are no shortcuts on the critical path — but you can run everything else in parallel.
Parallel tracks — run these while waiting for COFEPRIS
COFEPRIS takes 3–9 months. Smart operators use that time to be fully ready to open the day the license arrives.
🏗
Buildout
Complete lab construction and equipment installation. Must be ready before inspection.
🔬
Equipment
Order analyzers early — import lead times are 8–16 weeks. Calibrate before inspection.
👥
Staffing
Hire and train QFB, lab techs, and front desk. IMSS registration once staff is signed.
🩺
Physician outreach
Start visiting médicos now. Takes 3–5 touches. Your referral network should be warm before day 1.
💻
LIS & branding
Set up LIS software, WhatsApp Business, Google Business Profile, logo, and signage.
🎯
Goal
Be 100% operational the day the Licencia Sanitaria arrives. No scrambling.
Key milestones
COFEPRIS application filed Month 3
Triggers the inspection clock. Every day you delay filing is a day you delay opening.
Equipment installed & calibrated Month 8
All analyzers must be on-site and calibrated before COFEPRIS arrives. Inspector will check them.
COFEPRIS inspection Month 9
Physical inspection of the lab. Have all documents ready: QFB cédula, equipment certs, RPBI contract, floor plan.
Licencia Sanitaria received Month 9–10
Green light to operate. Post the original visibly in the lab — inspectors will check for it.
Soft launch — first patient Month 10
Revenue begins. Target 50–80 studies in month 1, break-even by month 6–8.

Federal requirements (COFEPRIS)
Licencia Sanitaria
Core operating license. Requires: QFB as Director Técnico, physical inspection, equipment validated, RPBI plan in place
Est. cost: $5,000–15,000 MXN · Time: 3–9 months
→
Aviso de Funcionamiento
Online filing via SIVISAM portal. Must be done before opening
Est. cost: Minimal · Time: 1–2 weeks
→
NOM-007-SSA3-2011
Lab infrastructure: space, areas de recepción, toma de muestra, análisis. Min 60m²
→
NOM-166-SSA1-1997
Quality, procedures, and equipment calibration for clinical labs
→
NOM-087-SEMARNAT-SSA1-2002
RPBI (biohazardous waste): separation, labeling, transport contracts with authorized carrier
→
Permiso de Publicidad COFEPRIS
Autorización para publicidad de servicios médicos bajo la Ley General de Salud. Requerido antes de anunciarte
Est. cost: $1,500–4,000 MXN · Time: 4–8 weeks
→
NOM-059-SSA1-2013
Buenas prácticas de fabricación para análisis clínicos — SOPs, trazabilidad, control de calidad
→
NOM-050-SCFI-2004
Etiquetado de recipientes, tubos y muestras — información comercial y sanitaria requerida
→
LFPDPPP — Datos personales
Ley Federal de Protección de Datos Personales. Aviso de privacidad obligatorio para pacientes
→

Director Técnico requirement
This is the single most critical hire. COFEPRIS will not issue a Licencia Sanitaria without a named QFB with cédula profesional on file.
QFB (Químico Farmacéutico Biólogo)
Cédula profesional registered with Dirección General de Profesiones
Can be part-time or shared
Some small labs contract a QFB part-time. Salary: $18,000–35,000 MXN/mo full-time

36-month revenue vs. costs
Based on current Monthly P&L inputs · launch at month 1
Annual summary
Period Revenue ⓘ
Revenue
Studies × avg ticket price
Includes patient (direct) + corporate streams
Ramp applied in Year 1: 40% → 65% → 85% of target volume. Full volume from Year 2.
 Total Costs ⓘ
Total operating costs
Payroll (×1.48 IMSS burden) + Reagents + Rent + Utilities + Admin
Payroll uses a fixed headcount model. Reagents scale with study volume at the configured % of revenue.
 EBITDA ⓘ
EBITDA
Revenue − Total Costs
Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation & Amortization. Measures core operational profitability before accounting adjustments.
 Margin ⓘ
EBITDA margin
EBITDA ÷ Revenue × 100
Healthy range for a clinical lab: 20–35%. Below 0% = not yet viable at that volume.
 ISR 30% ⓘ
ISR provision (30%)
30% × positive EBITDA (simplified provision)
Equipment depreciation reduces taxable base
Personas Morales — Régimen General (Art. 9 LISR). Actual ISR will differ once deductions, PTU, and depreciation schedules are applied. Consult your contador.
 Net Income ⓘ
Net income (after ISR)
EBITDA − ISR provision
After-tax profit available to the company. Drives the cumulative cash position each year.
 Cum. Cash ⓘ
Cumulative cash position
Starts at −Startup Investment
+= Net Income each year
Turns positive when the startup investment is fully recovered. The year it crosses zero is your payback milestone.
📊 Ramp assumption: Year 1 months 1–3 at 40% volume, months 4–6 at 65%, months 7–12 at 85%. Year 2 at 100%. Year 3 at 110% (growth). Adjust monthly volumes in the Financial Calculator to change these projections.
📋 ISR 30% is calculated on positive EBITDA as a simplified provision (Personas Morales — Régimen General). Actual ISR may differ based on deductions, depreciation, and PTU. Consult your contador for exact figures.

Pricing strategy summary
Bundle opportunities
Perfil Básico (checkup): BHC + QS6 + EGO + lipídico. Individual sum: ~$860. Bundle at $599 — 30% discount feels like a deal, avg ticket goes up vs. single-test visits.
Perfil Tiroideo Completo: TSH + T3 + T4 + T4 libre. Individual sum: ~$920. Bundle at $699. High demand from endocrinologists.
Check-up Empresarial: BHC + QS12 + EGO + lipídico + prueba antidoping (5 panel). Bundle at $799 per employee. Volume play for corporate contracts.

1
Research & Planning
Months 1–2· In progress· Est. cost: $15,000–30,000 MXN
Why this matters: Everything downstream depends on getting this right. Click any task below to expand its workspace — check off sub-steps, add notes, and attach files. Your progress drives the Phase 1 bar on the dashboard.
Core tasks
Deliverables when phase is complete
Competitive analysis document (zone-by-zone)
Business model canvas (revenue channels defined)
3-year financial model (3 scenarios)
Shortlist of 3 locations with uso de suelo status
Test menu v1 with equipment requirements
Pricing strategy (tier positioning defined)
Key decisions to make
General vs. specialty?
General labs have broader demand but thinner margins. Specialty (e.g., hormonal panels, molecular) commands higher tickets but needs more expensive equipment and a wider referral base. Recommended: start general, layer specialty at month 12–18.
Own vs. lease equipment?
Many reagent companies (Roche, Beckman, Mindray) offer comodato: free analyzer in exchange for reagent exclusivity. This slashes startup cost but locks you in. Good for year 1, renegotiate after.
Referral lab partnership?
For tests you won't run in-house (PCR, specialized cultures, genetic), partner with a referral lab like Carpermor or Quest Mexico. You draw the sample, they run it, you keep the margin on the patient-facing price.
Querétaro-specific tips
Best zones to research: Juriquilla/Zibatá (high income, low competition), Satélite/Epigmenio (dense residential, IMSS overflow), and Centro/Constituyentes (high foot traffic, physician offices).

Corporate channel: Querétaro's industrial parks (El Marqués, Aeropuerto) house 300+ manufacturing plants required by NOM to provide annual employee health screenings. This is a massive untapped B2B channel.
⚡ Go / No-Go Decision Gate
Before committing capital to Phase 2, all criteria must be met. Use the Go/No-Go page.
2
Legal & Corporate Setup
Months 2–4· To do· Est. cost: $30,000–60,000 MXN
Critical path: You cannot apply for COFEPRIS permits without a legally constituted empresa and RFC. Click any task to expand its workspace.
Core tasks
Deliverables when phase is complete
Acta Constitutiva (notarized)
Pacto de Socios (if partners involved)
RFC registration confirmation
e.firma (electronic signature) active
Business bank account open
Signed lease with uso de suelo confirmed
CFDI invoicing setup (PAC provider selected)
Professional liability insurance policy
Key decisions to make
S.A. de C.V. vs S.A.S.?
S.A. de C.V. is standard for clinical labs — liability protection, investor-ready, expected by COFEPRIS. S.A.S. is simpler but has capital limits. Go S.A. de C.V.
Need a Pacto de Socios?
If taking on ANY partner: yes. Cover vesting, decision rights, profit distribution, exit mechanisms. Draft BEFORE the Acta Constitutiva. $8K-$20K MXN for a specialized attorney.
Which insurance?
RC Profesional (diagnostic errors), RC General (premises), Equipment (fire/theft/earthquake), Employee accident. Budget $40K-$80K/yr total. GNP, AXA, Zurich — bundle for 10-15% discount.

COFEPRIS & NOM Permits
Months 3–9· To do· Est. cost: $20,000–80,000 MXN
Longest and most unpredictable phase. COFEPRIS timelines range from 4 to 12 months. Click tasks to track your progress on each requirement.
Core tasks
Deliverables when phase is complete
Director Técnico (QFB) under contract
Aviso de Funcionamiento accepted
Licencia Sanitaria application filed
NOM-007 compliant floor plan
NOM-087 RPBI waste management plan
Protección Civil dictamen received
COFEPRIS inspection passed
Licencia Sanitaria in hand
Key decisions to make
Full-time vs. part-time QFB?
COFEPRIS requires a named QFB. Full-time ($28-35K/mo) gives you on-site quality control. Some labs start with a part-time arrangement, but this limits your hours and inspection flexibility.
Hire a gestor for COFEPRIS?
A regulatory consultant ($15-30K) who knows the process can save months. They know what inspectors look for and can pre-audit your lab. Worth it for first-time lab operators.
Critical timeline
COFEPRIS is the longest and most variable step. Typical timeline:
Month 1: File Aviso de Funcionamiento
Month 1-2: Prepare Licencia Sanitaria application
Month 2: Submit application
Month 3-8: Wait for inspection scheduling
Month 8-9: Pass inspection (or correct and re-inspect)
Month 9-12: Receive Licencia Sanitaria
4
Infrastructure & Equipment
Months 5–10· To do· Est. cost: $400,000–1,200,000 MXN
Run in parallel with COFEPRIS. Order equipment early — import lead times are 8–16 weeks. Your lab must be ready before the inspection.
Core tasks
Deliverables when phase is complete
Lab space fully built out per NOM-007
All analyzers installed and calibrated
Cold chain operational (2-8C, -20C)
LIS configured and tested
Furniture, fixtures, and signage installed
IT infrastructure (network, printers, backup)
Key decisions to make
Buy vs. comodato?
Comodato: free analyzer, locked to one reagent vendor. Slashes startup cost by $300-800K but locks you in for 3-5 years. Good for year 1 — renegotiate after volume proves out.
Which LIS?
SaaS ($3-8K/mo) vs. on-premise license ($50-150K). SaaS is recommended — lower upfront, automatic updates, WhatsApp integration. Must support CFDI 4.0 and Spanish-language reports.
New vs. refurbished equipment?
Refurbished hematology/chemistry analyzers can save 40-60%. Ensure warranty, calibration certificates, and reagent availability. Mindray offers competitive new-equipment pricing for emerging markets.

5
Staffing & Training
Months 7–12· To do· Est. cost: $80,000–200,000 MXN
Hire and train before day one. Your QFB must be on-site for the COFEPRIS inspection. Lab techs need 2–4 weeks of equipment training.
Core tasks
Deliverables when phase is complete
All staff hired and IMSS-registered
Training logs signed by each employee
SOPs drafted and approved by QFB
Daily QC procedures running
PACAL/EQC enrollment confirmed
LIS proficiency verified for all users
Key decisions to make
Minimum viable team?
4 people: QFB (director), 1 quimico analista, 1 flebotomista, 1 recepcionista. Add a second lab tech at ~200 studies/month. Cleaning can be outsourced initially.
PACAL vs. RIQAS vs. Bio-Rad?
PACAL is the most recognized in Mexico and costs $15-25K/year. RIQAS and Bio-Rad EQAS are international alternatives. COFEPRIS accepts all three. Start with PACAL for simplicity.

Soft Launch & Marketing
Months 9–18· To do· Est. cost: $30,000–80,000 MXN
Revenue starts here. Your physician referral network should be warm before day 1. Start visiting médicos 2–3 months before opening.
Core tasks
Deliverables when phase is complete
30+ physician offices visited
Price list finalized (público + médico)
Google Business Profile live and verified
WhatsApp Business configured for result delivery
First corporate contract signed
Grand opening event completed
First 30 days of operations data
Key decisions to make
Launch with or without toma a domicilio?
Home collection adds cost ($10-15K/mo for a dedicated flebotomista + vehicle). Wait until you have 40+ domicilio requests/month to break even. Use the Toma a Domicilio calculator in the app.
Soft launch first?
Yes. Open 2 weeks before grand opening with limited hours and invite-only patients. Use this to shake out LIS bugs, QC issues, and workflow bottlenecks.
Opening discount?
10-20% off for the first month drives volume and word-of-mouth. Don\'t discount to physician-referred patients — the médico discount is already applied.
Querétaro-specific tips
Physician visits work best 8-10am and 1-3pm — between their patient blocks. Bring a printed price list (público + médico tiers), a sample lab report, and business cards.

Google Business Profile is the #1 way walk-in patients find you. Upload 10+ photos, set hours, add your test menu and prices. Respond to every review within 24 hours.
7
Operations & Growth
Months 12–18+· To do· Post-launch · Ongoing
You're open for business. This phase covers daily operations, quality management, tax compliance, revenue growth, and working capital. These tasks repeat and evolve — they're not one-time checkboxes.
Core tasks
Key milestones
Month 1: All daily QC protocols running without gaps
Month 1: First CFDI invoices issued successfully
Month 2: First corporate health contract activated
Month 3: Operational audit complete — volume, TAT, QC metrics
Month 3: PACAL first proficiency test submitted
Month 3: Revenue mix review — actual vs projected by channel
Month 6: Toma a domicilio evaluation (launch if 40+ requests/mo)
Month 12: Annual ISR declaration prepared
Key metrics to track weekly
Volume: Studies/day by channel (walk-in, physician, corporate). Target: ramp to 300/month by Month 6 post-launch.
TAT: % of results delivered within 4 hours. Your #1 differentiator. Track daily, review weekly.
Cash: Weekly cash balance vs. projection. Never drop below 3× monthly operating costs.
AR Aging: Corporate receivables >60 days. Follow up immediately on anything overdue.

Mexico funding landscape
NAFIN — Nacional Financiera
Up to $2M MXN, 10–14% annual, 12–84 months. Via BBVA/Banamex/Banorte intermediaries. Requires solid business plan for new ventures.
SE — Fondo PyME / FAMPYME
Government grants and subsidies for SMEs in strategic sectors. Health services qualify. Non-reimbursable grants of $50K–$500K MXN. Competitive application.
Fondeadora / Doopla — Crowdfunding
Mexican regulated crowdfunding platforms (CNBV-regulated). Good for community-backed health projects. 10–18% effective rate for debt crowdfunding.
Angel / socio capitalista
Silent partner common in Mexican healthcare. Typically 20–40% equity stake for $500K–$1.5M MXN. Define roles, profit split, and exit in Acta Constitutiva.

Break-even chart
Revenue vs. total costs as volume increases — base case (dashed) vs. scenario (solid)
How to read this chart
The green line shows monthly revenue as your study volume grows. The red line shows total costs — fixed costs (rent, payroll, utilities, insurance) plus variable costs (reagents, scaling with volume). Where they cross is your break-even volume. Below that: a loss; above: profit. The dashed blue line shows profit directly. When scenario adjustments are active, solid lines show the adjusted model while dashed lines show the base case for comparison.

¿Cuánto colchón de efectivo necesitas entre pagar proveedores y cobrar a pacientes?
Why this matters: Reagent suppliers want payment in 30–60 days. Walk-in patients pay same-day, but corporate contracts pay in 45–90 days. The gap between cash out and cash in is your working capital requirement — underfund it and you can't buy reagents even while profitable on paper.

Gestión de calidad (SGC)
SOPs, procedimientos de QC, auditorías internas y participación en EQC — lo que COFEPRIS realmente inspecciona
Why this matters: COFEPRIS doesn't just check that you have equipment — they check that you have a documented quality system. NOM-166-SSA1-1997 requires written SOPs for every test, calibration logs, internal QC records, external quality assessment (EQC/PACAL) participation, and staff competency documentation. Building this from day one also positions you for future ISO 15189 accreditation, which significantly helps with corporate contracts.
